title: Cross-functional dependability sprint heuristics and comms diary
content:
Purpose:
This document is a working sprint diary and tactical checklist for a 10-week cross-functional dependability program focused on defining and operationalizing SLOs for model-serving endpoints. It’s intentionally informal — notes, hypotheses, comms templates, and handoff scripts we can iterate in the open.

Background/context: quick bullets
- Goal: get 6 product-serving teams to a baseline SLO (latency P95 and error-rate) + runbooks + rollout gating within 10 weeks.
- Motivation: recent production regressions in hosted API (Dec 2025) highlighted gaps: inconsistent ownership, missing observability for model variants, and unclear rollback policies.
- Success criteria (working): onboarded teams show a measurable drop in P95 tail and a documented runbook; at least 2 teams use canary + automatic fallback.

High-level approach
1) Week 0-2: discovery + telemetry hardening
   - Audit: each service/microservice owning model endpoints (list owners and current signal coverage)
   - Fill telemetry gaps: add request-id propagation, tokenized latency buckets, KV-cache hit metrics; short spike alert M: SRE-telemetry-ops
   - Deliverable: minimal observability checklist per team + shared dashboard template

2) Week 3-6: SLO design + experiment lab
   - Run SLO design workshops with product & infra: define consumer-impact metrics (auth failure vs model runtime error), map to error budget policy
   - Hypotheses: 1) prefix caching reduces P95 by 15% for chat-heavy routes. 2) Route-level failover to quantized model reduces error-rate at cost of quality degradation detectable by evals.
   - Small experiments: enable prefix cache for 15% of traffic on test cluster; pilot quantized variant in a canary pool.
   - Deliverable: SLO config PRs (repo: infra/slo-config), experiment result log, decision flags (promote/rollback)

3) Week 7-10: rollout + handoff + runbooks
   - Canary-to-gradual rollouts with automatic fallback per policy (traffic split, thresholds, time windows)
   - Oncall handoff runbooks: escalation tree, verification script, rollback playbook (short commands + run outputs)
   - Post-mortem template and acceptance checklist for SLO adoption
   - Deliverable: per-service runbook in docs repo, merged SLO configs, training session recordings

Operational heuristics (quick reference)
- SLO composition: prefer consumer-impact over infrastructure-only signals. If consumer signal missing, create a proxy signal (e.g., inference-response-with-error-field).
- Error budget policy: soft-threshold alert at 40% burn in 1h, action at 70% burn in 6h (notify product + SRE), auto-fallback trigger at 90% burn for 15m window.
- Latency SLOs: use P95 for interactive routes, P99 for batch inference endpoints.
- Canary windows: 30m ramp for new model variant, require <10% relative increase in error-rate and <5% P95 regression to proceed to 2h ramp.

Cross-functional roles + responsibilities (working)
- Product owner (PO): clarifies customer-impact windows and approves SLO targets; owns rollback decision when quality tradeoffs hit.
- SRE lead: owns observability baseline, alerting, runbook template, and rollout automation.
- Serving-runtime eng: provides model variants, quantization flags, and in-cluster routing hooks.
- Data/Quality (ML): evaluates model-quality deltas for fallback decisions, maintains eval suites.
- Solutions/Support: coordinates customer communications and incident comms templates.

Communication plan (templates + cadence)
- Weekly 30m sync: Tue 10:00 PT — 15m cross-team status + 15m blockers escalation. Owner: Maya.
- Daily short-run calls only during canary windows for teams in rollout (ops bridge).
- Stakeholder digest: concise status update every Friday with: teams onboarded, open experiments, action items, next week asks. Use PRD email template below.

PRD email template (short):
Subject: [Dependability sprint] Week {n} status — teams X/Y onboarded, canaries running
Body: TL;DR (1-2 lines), Key metrics (P95, error-rate change, error-budget burn), Open blockers (owner + ETA), Ask for leadership (approval/extra runway)

Handoff scripts (example snippets)
- Quick verify a canary health (to run from bastion):
  - curl -H \"x-correlation-id: test-verify\" https://svc.example/api/v1/infer?model=variant-canary | jq '.latency, .status'
  - query dashboards: last_30m P95 with tag variant=canary (grafana link)
- Rollback (automated): toggle traffic-split --set variant=stable --duration=30m --reason \"canary-failed-slo\" (CLI alias: rtw rollback)

Experiment log template (one-line per experiment)
- id: EXP-2026-01-cach-01
- owner: Ethan Brooks
- hypothesis: prefix caching reduces P95 by >=10% for chat routes
- config: cache=true, ttl=30s, rollout=15%
- outcome: P95 -12% (pass), KV-hit 42%
- note: observed slight CPU increase on worker nodes; SRE to review autoscaler thresholds

Risks & mitigation (raw brainstorm)
- Risk: observability gaps delay diagnosis -> Mitigation: baseline telemetry must be gated step before any canaries
- Risk: quality regressions when falling back to quantized models -> Mitigation: require per-traffic evals and a manual PO sign-off for persistent fallback longer than 1h
- Risk: lack of owner follow-through for runbook edits -> Mitigation: assign runbook ownership in oncall rotation roster and link PR to weekly digest

Open questions (to resolve in first workshop)
- What is the minimum acceptable SLO per product tier (free vs paid vs enterprise)?
- Which quality metric best maps to customer-visible degradation for model outputs? (BLEU-ish metrics are noisy)
- Should we centralize SLO configs in infra repo or allow team-level overriding with guardrails?

Next immediate actions (this doc as TODO backlog)
- [Maya] schedule initial SLO design workshop (invite: SRE leads, PO reps, serving eng, data/quality) — due 2026-01-22
- [Ethan] run telemetry audit for 4 candidate services and share template — due 2026-01-25
- [Sofia] draft canary rollback CLI alias and helm chart snippet — due 2026-01-28
- [Liam] prepare evaluation harness for quantized variant (small dataset) — due 2026-02-01

Notes to self / rough thoughts (scratchpad)
- We should try a "dependability blitz" day: 1 full-day pairing with product teams to close observability gaps (pair by pairing setup: SRE + product + infra).
- Consider adding a lightweight monthly "SLO health" KPI to the org dashboard showing percentage of services with current runbooks.
- Keep runbook short — list only 5 things to check first (traffic, errors, recent deploys, KV cache hit, fallback status).

References / links (working)
- Confluence: reliability-framework-onramp (linked above)
- GitHub: infra/slo-config (pattern examples)
- Slack threads: #sre-ops \"dec-2025-production-incidents\"

Appendix: quick runbook template (minimal)
- Service name:
- Owner (oncall rotation):
- SLO target (latency/error):
- Primary dashboard link:
- First 5 checks (with commands):
- Auto-fallback policy snippet:
- Post-incident actions: TODO

---
This doc is iterative; add experiment outcomes and short notes here as they happen. If something looks like it should be pulled into a more formal playbook, tag \"formalize\" and we’ll escalate to the playbook repo.
